title: Micron Bounces Back, Yet Goldman Highlights Top Memory Picks Over Its Revival
body:
Micron Technology’s shares rallied on Wednesday, snapping a recent slide and drawing the attention of value‑oriented investors, but analysts at Goldman Sachs cautioned that the broader memory‑chip market still offers more compelling opportunities. The investment bank highlighted South Korea’s SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics as the sector’s better‑priced bets, suggesting that Micron’s bounce may be more of a short‑term correction than a sign of a sustained turnaround.

The 2.5 percent gain in Micron’s stock came after the company reported a modest beat on its second‑quarter earnings, driven by higher demand for DRAM in data‑center servers and a slight uptick in automotive applications. Revenue rose 4 percent year‑over‑year to $7.1 billion, while adjusted earnings per share edged up to $0.71, surpassing analysts’ consensus of $0.68. Management also hinted at progress in its 3‑nanometer process, which could improve yield and reduce costs in the coming years. These developments helped to ease concerns that the company was lagging behind its rivals in a market that has been volatile since the pandemic‑induced boom.

Despite the positive numbers, Goldman’s senior technology strategist, Andrew Feldman, argued that Micron’s valuation remains stretched relative to its peers. “Even with the recent price appreciation, Micron trades at a forward‑price‑to‑earnings multiple that is still higher than the historical average for the memory segment,” Feldman said in a note to clients. “SK Hynix and Samsung, on the other hand, are trading at significant discounts to their own 12‑month earnings outlooks, offering a better risk‑adjusted entry point.” The bank’s analysis points to Samsung’s dominant position in NAND flash, where it holds roughly 35 percent of global capacity, and SK Hynix’s aggressive expansion in high‑bandwidth memory (HBM), a technology increasingly critical for AI workloads.

Industry dynamics reinforce Goldman’s perspective. The memory market is currently in a cyclical trough, with global DRAM inventories running near 13 percent above the five‑year average, according to data from the Semiconductor Industry Association. Prices for both DRAM and NAND have been under pressure for several quarters, and analysts expect a gradual price recovery only as new product cycles—particularly AI‑optimized chips—gain traction. Samsung and SK Hynix are better positioned to capitalize on this shift because of their larger scale, more diversified product portfolios, and stronger cash flows, which enable sustained investment in next‑generation manufacturing nodes.

Investors who are drawn to Micron’s recent bounce should weigh the company’s specific risks. The firm’s reliance on a single fab in Singapore makes it vulnerable to geopolitical tensions in the Indo‑Pacific region, while its relatively smaller market share limits pricing power during inventory drawdowns. Moreover, Micron’s roadmap for 3‑nanometer DRAM is still several years away, meaning the company must navigate a competitive landscape where rivals may already be delivering higher‑density, lower‑cost solutions.

Looking ahead, the memory sector is likely to be shaped by the accelerating adoption of artificial‑intelligence workloads, edge computing, and the rollout of 5G infrastructure. Companies that can secure a foothold in high‑bandwidth memory and next‑generation NAND will stand to benefit from the anticipated surge in demand for data‑intensive applications. While Micron’s recent earnings beat and modest share price rally provide a momentary lift, analysts suggest that a more prudent strategy may involve allocating capital to the better‑valued South Korean giants, which appear poised to capture a larger slice of the upcoming growth wave. As the market steadies, investors will be watching closely whether Micron can translate its technical progress into sustainable earnings momentum or whether the sector’s broader valuation dynamics will continue to favor its larger, more diversified peers.
